::: {.why}
Nothing that follows works if you do not know what the vendor did to the history, and the adjustment is the single most common silent error in retail-grade backtests.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State the arithmetic a vendor performs on the whole history when a dividend is paid, and what that does to the level of prices ten years ago.
- Name two analyses that adjusted prices silently break, and say what you would use instead for each.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Reconstruct the adjustment yourself. From the unadjusted SPY closes plus the dividend and split history, build your own back-adjusted series and check it matches yfinance's `auto_adjust=True` close to within rounding. When it does not match, the discrepancy is the interesting part.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [15 min]{.task-min} Now break it deliberately: compute the number of shares 10,000 dollars would have bought in 2005 using the adjusted series, and using the unadjusted series. One of those numbers is meaningless. Say which and why, in two sentences in the notebook.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Add to the glossary: the two analyses adjusted prices break. Dollar volume and any price-level rule such as a 5 dollar minimum are the two to name.
:::
:::
